messages:
zoe: onboarding a customer onto Dedicated and hit a confusing SSL/proxy combo with the py async SDK. sync worked and our quickstart used the sync snippet, but async fails for their env. anyone document this pattern?

emily: what's the failure? quick example of how they're running it?

zoe: error is `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: unable to get local issuer certificate` from httpx/httpcore. they're on corp infra with HTTPS interception and we asked them to set REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL to the private endpoint and mount their CA at /etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem. sync client ok, async no.

kevin: likely parity gap: async constructor currently doesn't expose ca_bundle/verify/trust_env like sync does and builds an SSLContext from certifi by default. causes env vars like SSL_CERT_FILE or HTTPS_PROXY (with trust_env) to be ignored.

ravi: also saw reports of weird retries — their infra saw multiple repeated attempts in logs for a cert problem. seems our retry layer retries some SSL/transport errors which just confuses customers.

emily: couple of priorities: (1) API parity — add `ca_bundle: Optional[Union[str, Path]]`, `trust_env: Optional[bool]`, and `proxies` to AsyncClient; (2) env fallback — prefer explicit param > SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE > certifi; (3) retry behavior — default `retry_on_ssl=false` so cert failures surface immediately; (4) typing + examples so mypy + DX are good.

kevin: implementation note: forward `verify` to httpx.AsyncClient or build an SSLContext that loads the file. cache SSLContext per verify-path to avoid per-connection allocation. also respect trust_env for proxy environments; for Dedicated default `trust_env=True` if HTTPS_PROXY present.

zoe: for onboarding docs we should show three reproducible checks: httpx one-liner, openssl s_client, and python snippet with raw httpx.AsyncClient so customers can rule out SDK wrapper:```bash
# httpx quick check
export HTTPS_PROXY=https://corp-proxy.local:443
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem
python - <<'PY'
import httpx
print(httpx.get('https://redwood.private.internal', verify='/etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem').status_code)
PY
```

ravi: typing UX is real — folks try to pass `verify` through kwargs and hit mypy errors. please add explicit typed args rather than a catch-all `**kwargs`. good autocomplete is worth the small API expansion.

kevin: agree. adding typed args also helps us document semantics in docstrings. will also add unit + mypy tests: precedence, proxy+trust_env behavior, pooled connection with custom CA, and a test that SSLCertVerificationError is not retried by default.

ci-bot: created issue #6122: "py-sdk: async client parity for ca_bundle/proxy/trust_env + disable ssl retries by default" and linked this thread.

emily: UX note: add a short sample-app in examples/async-dedicated that demonstrates systemd and k8s manifests showing env var mounts for CA and REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL. people repeatedly forget to mount the CA or set the base_url so this will cut support tickets.

zoe: yes please — also include a troubleshooting checklist in onboarding playbook: check base_url, mount CA, run httpx one-liner, try raw httpx.AsyncClient, and capture first-failure stack (don't rely on retries).

kevin: i'll draft PR with minimal, backward-compatible change: add new optional args to AsyncClient, wire to httpx, add tests, update docs + examples, and set retry_on_ssl default false. ping when draft is up.

emily: once PR is up we'll ask a couple of customers to smoke test in corp proxy setups. also prepare a short changelog line and a small migration note for Dedicated users.

zoe: huge help, thanks. this will reduce onboarding friction a lot. :rocket:
